parsed_answer.content: In the Spring Framework, @Transactional isolation levels define the boundary of data visibility between concurrent database transactions. These levels are a direct abstraction of the SQL standard, designed to mitigate three primary concurrency anomalies: Dirty Reads, Non-repeatable Reads, and Phantoms. READ_UNCOMMITTED is the lowest isolation level, allowing a transaction to see uncommitted changes from others; while it offers maximum performance, it is rarely used in production due to the risk of reading data that might be rolled back. READ_COMMITTED, the default for most RDBMS like PostgreSQL and SQL Server, prevents dirty reads by ensuring only committed data is visible. REPEATABLE_READ ensures that if you read a row twice, the data remains consistent, blocking other transactions from modifying it, though it may still allow phantom reads. Finally, SERIALIZABLE is the strictest level; it forces transactions to execute as if they were running sequentially, usually through range-locking or optimistic concurrency control, effectively eliminating all anomalies at the cost of significant throughput degradation.

items: Spring's @Transactional annotation delegates isolation to the underlying DataSource's connection object. When a method is invoked, the TransactionManager retrieves a connection and explicitly sets the isolation level via Connection.setTransactionIsolation(int).

REPEATABLE_READ in MySQL (InnoDB) uses Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) to provide a consistent snapshot of the database at the start of the transaction, which is why it inherently avoids phantom reads in InnoDB, even though the SQL standard technically allows them.

SERIALIZABLE often triggers deadlocks in high-concurrency environments because the database engine must acquire range locks on index gaps to prevent phantom inserts, leading to contention that can bring a microservice to a crawl.

Changing isolation levels at the method level via @Transactional(isolation = Isolation.SERIALIZABLE) overrides the default global configuration of the connection pool, which can lead to unexpected performance bottlenecks if applied to high-traffic read operations.

parsed_answer.content: Senior Engineer Insight: Never assume the database driver supports all levels. For example, some cloud-native databases or specific configurations of NoSQL-backed SQL interfaces may silently ignore certain isolation settings. Always verify the actual transaction isolation level in your logs using 'SELECT @@transaction_isolation' or equivalent if you experience non-deterministic behavior in high-load scenarios.

title: Explain @Transactional Isolation levels (READ_UNCOMMITTED, READ_COMMITTED, REPEATABLE_READ, SERIALIZABLE).
